title: Pub/sub, queues and fan-out
idea: In pub/sub, a publisher sends a message to a topic and every subscriber receives a copy. A queue instead gives each message to one consumer.
points: A queue shares work: each message goes to one consumer.
A topic broadcasts: the publisher does not know who subscribes.
Fan-out means one event reaching many independent consumers, each at its own pace.
Common design: a topic feeds one queue per subscriber, and workers share each queue.

steps.caption: The orders service publishes one `order.placed` event to the topic. It does not know who listens.
The topic gives every subscription its own copy of the event.
Each subscriber reads from its own queue, so slow analytics does not delay billing.
Later, a fraud-check subscriber joins. The publisher does not change at all.

code.title: Topic and queue side by side
code.caption: An `EventEmitter` acts as a topic. A shared array acts as a queue. Add a fourth subscriber and run again.

pitfalls: Use a queue, not a topic, for a job only one worker should do.
A new subscriber may not see past events; check whether your messaging system keeps them.
Each subscriber's queue can still redeliver, so each handler must be idempotent.

quiz.why: `emit` calls every listener in the order they were registered, like a topic. Each `shift` takes a different job, like a queue.

takeaway: Queues share work between workers; topics copy each event to every subscriber.

starters: What happens to a message when a subscriber is offline?
